summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as root:root mode 1777 (world-writable with sticky bit), verified two distinct non-root users can each create files but cannot delete each other's files while retaining the ability to delete their own. Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (real restart, not just downtime), and re-verified /srv/drop's permissions and cross-user delete-protection behavior post-restart.
actions_performed: Set mode 1777 on /srv/drop (rwxrwxrwt with sticky bit)
Created test users dropuserA and dropuserB
Verified each user can create files in /srv/drop
Verified dropuserB cannot delete dropuserA's file (Operation not permitted) while dropuserA can delete its own file
Captured baseline boot_id and directory state on node1
Issued sudo -n systemctl reboot on node1, confirmed connection drop as acknowledgement
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop mode/ownership and re-ran the cross-user delete-protection functional test post-restart, cleaning up test artifacts

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared directory with correct ownership/mode (1777)
evidence.summary: mkdir + chown root:root + chmod 1777; stat/ls -ld confirm '1777 root:root /srv/drop' and 'drwxrwxrwt. 2 root root 6 ... /srv/drop'

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement) — pre-restart
evidence.summary: dropuserA and dropuserB each created a file; dropuserB's attempt to rm dropuserA's file failed with 'Operation not permitted'; each user successfully deleted their own file

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before node1 restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be and confirmed /srv/drop mode/ownership (1777 root:root) prior to restart
Backgrounded 'sudo -n systemctl reboot' dispatched and acknowledged locally before the SSH connection was closed by the rebooting host

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node unreachable immediately after reboot (connection timed out), then came back with boot_id 9a507a78-9bd2-4f27-b826-4ee10eaa6366, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and behavior
evidence.summary: Post-restart stat/ls -ld shows unchanged '1777 root:root /srv/drop'; repeated cross-user test shows dropuserB still denied deletion of dropuserA's file post-restart, confirming persistence of the sticky-directory configuration
